title: After strong shaking, rain-free Chilean streams stayed about 30% above their recession to day 60 and then followed their own recession (CAMELS-CL 1979-2016, mostly Maule 2010)
abstract: Question: How long does the stream flow excess after strong earthquake shaking last, and after its peak does the flow follow the catchment's normal recession (one pulse of water added to storage), stay above it (continued supply) or fall below it (faster drainage)? Earlier campaign studies (US sci:sha256:960bb4a1..., Chile sci:sha256:8abbb716...) could not find the end of the excess. Approach: For 491 CAMELS-CL gauges we fitted a daily dry-weather recession model from all rain-free days and used it as the counterfactual to day 90. Windows after declustered ComCat mainshocks were censored at the first CR2MET rain and compared with placebo windows at the same gauges in the same season of up to 30 other years. The plan was written before outcomes. Findings: At seismic energy density of 1 J/m3 or more (164 real windows, 19 events), the excess of mean ln Q over placebo was +0.18 on days 1-5, +0.27 on days 16-30 and +0.28 on days 31-60 (95% event-bootstrap interval +0.01 to +0.61, Holm p = 0.041; 44 windows, 8 events, 29 from Maule 2010). Without Maule the days 31-60 estimate was +0.17 (-0.05 to +0.77). Days 61-90 were not resolved (+0.19, -0.09 to +1.17; 15 windows). When the recession model was re-started from the flow at the peak, the residual on days peak+5 to peak+30 was -0.006 (-0.14 to +0.11; 68 windows), against +0.23 from the pre-event start. Thus the excess persists because flow starts from a higher store, and the gauges' own recession predicts a slow decay (half-life about 69 days). There was no excess at 0.1 to 1 J/m3. Limitations: Maule dominates the long windows; an injection test showed that the post-peak test cannot exclude a constant supply (+0.11) or a separate linear pulse (+0.08) of the observed size; gridded rain, regulated catchments, stepped low flows and a simple recession model.

display.caption: Top: daily excess of ln Q over each gauge's own recession counterfactual, earthquake windows minus placebo windows of the same events (7-day running mean), for e of 1 J/m3 or more (blue, with 95% event-bootstrap band), without Maule 2010 (orange) and for e of 0.1 to 1 J/m3 (green). Dashed: decay of the day-19 peak excess predicted by the gauges' own recession models. Bottom: number of rain-free earthquake windows on each day (log scale); curves are not shown below 10 windows.

Left (Q1): excess of mean ln Q by time block with 95% event-bootstrap intervals, for e of 1 J/m3 or more and without Maule; numbers give earthquake windows. Right (Q2): on days peak+5 to peak+30, the residual from the recession model started before the earthquake and from the model re-started at the peak (D2). Triangles: mean change of D2 when a synthetic constant supply or a synthetic separate linear pulse of the observed size is added to placebo windows.

Four real windows with the largest early rises and rain-free records to day 60: observed flow (black, ends at rain censoring), the recession counterfactual from day -2 (blue dashed), and the recession re-started at the peak (orange dashed).
